paragraphs: Clean Energy Fuels Corp., a Delaware corporation, is a leading renewable energy company focused on the procurement and distribution of renewable natural gas ("RNG") and conventional natural gas, in the form of compressed natural gas ("CNG") and liquefied natural gas ("LNG"), for the United States ("U.S.") and Canadian transportation markets. RNG, which is delivered as either CNG or LNG, is created by the recovery and processing of naturally occurring, environmentally detrimental waste methane ("biogas") from non-fossil fuel sources—such as dairy and other livestock waste and landfills—for environmentally beneficial use as a replacement for fossil-based transportation fuels at an affordable price. Methane is one of the most potent climate-harming greenhouse gases ("GHG") with a comparative impact on global warming that is about 28 times more powerful than that of carbon dioxide. We are focused on developing, owning, and operating dairy RNG projects and supplying RNG (currently procured from third party sources) to our customers in the heavy and medium-duty commercial transportation sectors. We have participated in the alternative vehicle fuels industry for over 28 years. We believe we are in a unique position because the valuable Environmental Credits (as defined below) are generated by the party that dispenses RNG into vehicle fuel tanks, and we believe we have access to more dispensers than any other market participant.
Clean Energy also sells bulk natural gas in the form of LNG and CNG to customers ranging from marine cargo ships to space aircraft to large paper mills.

We believe we were the first organization to sell RNG as a vehicle fuel in the U.S., and sales of our RNG for such purpose have increased from 13.0 million gasoline gallon equivalents ("GGEs") in 2013 to 237.4 million GGEs in 2025. We calculate one GGE to equal 125,000 British Thermal Units ("BTUs") and, as such, one million BTUs ("MMBTU") equals eight GGEs. We are North America's leading provider of the cleanest fuel for the commercial transportation market, based on both the number of stations we operate and the amount of GGEs serviced and GGEs sold of RNG, in the form of CNG and LNG, which amounted to a total of 468 million GGEs in 2025. With the Company's focus on RNG, our sales of RNG volume have grown from 12% of our vehicle fuel sales in 2013 to 88% of our vehicle fuel sales in 2025 (excluding GGEs from O&M (as defined below) services sales and non-vehicle sales). We believe that during 2025 we provided 50% and 32% of the RNG used for transportation fuel in California and the U.S., respectively.

As a comprehensive clean energy solutions provider, we also design and build, as well as operate and maintain ("O&M"), public and private vehicle fueling stations in the U.S. and Canada; transport and sell RNG and conventional natural gas via "virtual" natural gas pipelines and interconnects; sell U.S. federal, state and local government credits (collectively, "Environmental Credits") we generate by selling RNG as a vehicle fuel, including Renewable Identification Numbers ("RIN Credits" or "RINs") under the federal Renewable Fuel Standard Phase 2 and credits under the California, Oregon, New Mexico and Washington Low Carbon Fuel Standards (collectively, "LCFS Credits"); and obtain federal, state and local tax credits, grants and incentives. We serve fleet vehicle operators in a variety of markets, including heavy-duty trucking, airports, refuse, public transit, industrial and institutional energy users, and government fleets. We believe these fleet markets will continue to present a growth opportunity for our vehicle fuels for the foreseeable future.

Biogas, the primary source of RNG, is produced by microbes as they break down organic matter in the absence of oxygen. Our sources of commercial scale biogas are anaerobic digester gas ("ADG"), which is produced inside an airtight tank used to breakdown organic matter such as dairy and other livestock waste, and landfill gas ("LFG"), which is produced by the decomposition of organic waste at landfills.

Given the potential growth and positive environmental impact of RNG, our mission is to secure and sell as much RNG supply as possible. To that end we believe owning RNG facilities that provide a portion of our demand is beneficial. We do that on our own as well as through partnerships with TotalEnergies S.E. ("TotalEnergies"), BP Products North America ("bp") and Maas Energy. Further, we enter long-term RNG supply offtake agreements with well-known third parties that own RNG production facilities. Because our business transforms waste methane into a renewable source of energy, our RNG generates Environmental Credits under federal and state initiatives.

Depending on the source, the California Air Resources Board ("CARB") has determined that RNG can have a significantly negative carbon intensity score, enabling our customers to achieve a net carbon negative emissions profile.
California Air Resources Board "Current Fuel Pathways" 2025

At present, we see the best use of RNG as a replacement for fossil-based fuel, primarily diesel, being in the transportation sector. We believe the most attractive market for RNG is U.S. heavy-duty Class 8 trucking and, based on information from the American Trucking Association and our own internal estimates, we believe there are approximately 4.1 million Class 8 heavy-duty trucks operating in the U.S. that use over 40 billion gallons of fuel per year. As of December 31, 2025, we deliver RNG to the transportation market through 582 fueling stations we own, operate or supply in 43 states and the District of Columbia in the U.S., including over 200 stations in California. We also own, operate, or supply 27 fueling stations in Canada as of December 31, 2025. Critically, to generate Environmental Credits, the RNG must be placed in vehicle fuel tanks. We believe our stations and customer relationships allow us to sell substantially more RNG to vehicle operators than any other participant in the market – we calculate that we have access to more fueling stations and vehicle fleets than all our competitors combined. As of December 31, 2025, we served over 1,200 fleet customers operating over 65,000 vehicles on our fuels. We believe we are the only company in the U.S. that provides RNG vehicle fuel at scale in California and nationally.

Our principal products, services and other business activities are described below. Information about the revenue we receive from these activities is discussed in this report in Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations."
We sell RNG and conventional natural gas, in the form of CNG and LNG, as fuel for medium and heavy-duty vehicles.

● RNG is injected into natural gas pipelines, which allows RNG to be transported to vehicle fueling stations where it can be compressed and dispensed as CNG, and to liquefaction facilities where it is liquified and made into LNG. We source RNG from the DR JV (as defined below), and purchase RNG from bp and other third-party producers, comprising over 150 supply sources, typically under long-term RNG supply offtake agreements. In exchange for the agreement to offtake RNG supply, we and the supplier negotiate to determine what percentage share of the value of the Environmental Credit each party will retain. The value of the Environmental Credit is based on the realized value after the credit is sold to (purchased by) an obligated party or as agreed by the supplier and us as part of the negotiation. Our supply offtake agreements are variable and are based on actual RNG produced by the third-party producers, up to various maximum volume levels
as governed by the arrangement. In 2025, our third-party sourced RNG consisted of 40% ADG and 60% LFG.

Conventional natural gas is typically sourced from local utilities or third-party conventional natural gas marketers. We purchase conventional natural gas under North American Energy Standards Board base contracts on a spot market or short-term forward index basis or forward purchase contracts under take-or-pay arrangements that require us to purchase minimum volumes of conventional natural gas. Conventional natural gas is purchased on a normal purchase normal sale basis, as the conventional natural gas we purchase is for physical delivery of the commodity to our fueling stations for sale to customers.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business
Our success is dependent on the willingness of fleets and other customers to adopt our vehicle fuels, which may not occur in a timely manner, at expected levels or at all.
We are dependent on the production of vehicles and engines in our key customer and geographic markets by manufacturers, over which we have no control.
Our RNG business may not be successful.
Our commercial success depends on our ability and the ability of our third-party supply sources to successfully develop and operate projects and produce expected volumes of RNG.
To secure ADG RNG from new projects we develop, we typically face a long and variable development cycle that requires significant resource commitments and a long lead time before we realize revenue.
Livestock waste and dairy farm projects are dependent on LCFS credits and RINs.
We have a history of losses and may incur additional losses in the future.
Any potential future plans for hydrogen and electric vehicle stations may require significant cash investments and management resources and may not meet our expectations.
Increases, decreases and general volatility in the prices of RNG, natural gas, crude oil, diesel, renewable diesel and Environmental Credits could adversely affect our business.

We face increasing competition from competitors, many of which have far greater resources, customer bases and brand awareness than we have, and we may not be able to compete effectively with these businesses.
We rely on information technology in our operations, and any material failure, inadequacy, interruption, or security failure of that technology could harm our business.
NG Advantage may not be successful.
Our station construction activities subject us to business and operational risks.
We have significant contracts with government entities, which are subject to unique risks.
Our results of operations fluctuate significantly and are difficult to predict.
A pandemic, epidemic or other infectious disease outbreaks may adversely harm our business.
Our future success will depend on our ability to attract and retain qualified management, technical, and other personnel.
Risks Related to Our Indebtedness and Other Capital Resources.
We may need to raise additional capital to continue to fund our business, which could have negative effects and may not be available when needed, on acceptable terms or at all.
Our warranty reserves may not adequately cover our warranty obligations, which could result in unexpected costs.
Risks Related to Environmental Health and Safety and Governmental and Environmental Regulations

Our business is influenced by environmental, tax and other government regulations, programs and incentives that promote our vehicle fuels, and their modification or repeal could negatively affect our business.
To benefit from Environmental Credits, RNG projects are required to be registered and are subject to audit.
paragraphs: An investment in our Company involves a high degree of risk of loss. You should carefully consider the risk factors discussed below and all of the other information included in this report before you make any investment decision regarding our securities. We believe the risks and uncertainties described below are the most significant we face, but additional risks and uncertainties not known to us or that we currently deem immaterial could also be or become significant. The occurrence of any of these risks could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations, prospects and reputation and could cause the trading price of our common stock to decline.

Our success is highly dependent on the adoption by fleets and other customers of our RNG and conventional natural gas vehicle fuels. The market for our vehicle fuels has experienced slow, volatile and unpredictable growth in many sectors. For example, adoption and deployment of our vehicle fuels in heavy-duty trucking has been slower and more limited than we anticipated. Also, other important fleet markets, including airports, refuse, and public transit, had slower

volume and customer growth in recent years that may continue. If the market for our vehicle fuels does not develop at improved rates or levels, or if a market develops but we are not able to capture a significant share of the market or the market subsequently declines, our business, prospects, financial condition, and operating results would be harmed.

Factors that may influence the adoption of our vehicle fuels, many of which are beyond our control, include, among others: lack of demand for trucks that use our vehicle fuels; adoption or expansion of government policies, programs, funding or incentives, or increased publicity or popular sentiment in favor of vehicles or fuels other than RNG and natural gas, including long-standing support for diesel-powered vehicles, changes to emissions requirements applicable to vehicles and fleets powered by diesel, RNG, natural gas, or other vehicle fuels and/or growing support for renewable diesel, electric and hydrogen-powered vehicles; limitations on the capabilities of utilities to provide services to meet our requirements (for example, natural gas utilities may be unable to expand piping or provide services for new expansions, and electric utilities may lack the capacity to provide service for our projects); perceptions about the benefits of our vehicle fuels relative to diesel and other alternative vehicle fuels, including with respect to factors such as supply, cost savings, environmental benefits and safety; increases, decreases or volatility in the supply, demand, use and prices of crude oil, diesel, RNG, natural gas and other vehicle fuels, such as electricity, hydrogen, renewable diesel, biodiesel and ethanol; inertia among fleets and fleet vehicle operators, who may be unable or unwilling to prioritize converting a fleet to our vehicle fuels over an operator's other general business concerns, particularly if the operator is not sufficiently incentivized by emissions regulations or other requirements or lacks demand for the conversion from its customers, drivers, or other stakeholders; vehicle cost, fuel efficiency, availability, quality, safety, convenience (to fuel and service), design, performance and residual value, as well as operator perception with respect to these factors, generally and in our key customer markets and relative to comparable vehicles powered by other fuels; the development, production, cost, availability, performance, sales and marketing and reputation of engines that are well-suited for the vehicles used in our key customer markets, including heavy-duty trucks and other fleets; increasing competition in the market for vehicle fuels generally, and the nature and effect of competitive developments in this market, including improvements in or perceived advantages of other vehicle fuels and engines powered by these fuels; the impact of federal or state laws, orders or regulations mandating or in support of new or additional limits on GHG emissions, "tailpipe" emissions or internal combustion engines, including the ACT, the September 2020 Executive Order, the ACF regulation, the January 2025 Executive Order, and the June 2025 Executive Order (each as defined below); the availability and effect of environmental, tax or other government regulations, such as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ("OBBBA"), programs or incentives that promote our products or other alternatives as a vehicle fuel, including certain programs under which we generate credits by selling RNG as a vehicle fuel, as well as the market prices for such credits; and emissions and other environmental regulations and pressures on producing, transporting, and dispensing our fuels.

In addition, as our customers and partners react to economic conditions, such as tariffs, government shutdowns, and market volatility, and the potential for a recession, they may reduce spending and take additional precautionary measures to limit or delay expenditures and preserve capital and liquidity. Reductions in spending, delays in purchasing decisions, lack of renewals, inability to attract new customers, uncertainty about business continuity as well as pressure for extended billing terms or pricing discounts could limit our ability to grow our business and negatively affect our operating results and financial condition.

Vehicle and engine manufacturers control the development, production, quality assurance, cost and sales and marketing of their products, which shapes the performance, availability and reputation of these products in the marketplace. We are dependent on these manufacturers to succeed in our target markets, and we have no influence or control over their activities. A small number of manufacturers, chiefly Cummins, produce engines that use our vehicle fuels. The number of manufacturers making vehicles that use our fuels is limited as well. These manufacturers may decide not to expand or maintain, or may decide to discontinue or curtail, their engine or vehicle product lines for a variety of reasons, including as a result of the cost of development and production as a result of increased tariffs in the U.S. or retaliatory tariffs against the U.S., or adoption or modification of government policies or programs such as the ACT, the September 2020 Executive Order, the ACF, the January 2025 Executive Order and the OBBBA. The limited production of engines and vehicles that use our fuels increases their cost and limits availability, which restricts large-scale adoption, and may reduce resale value, which may contribute to operator reluctance to convert their fleets to vehicles that use our fuels. paragraphs: The following Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (this discussion, as well as discussions under the same heading in our other periodic reports, are referred to as the "MD&A") should be read together with our audited consolidated financial statements and the related notes included in this report, and all cross references to notes included in this MD&A refer to the identified note in such consolidated financial statements. This section of this report generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons of 2025 to 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons of 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this report can be found in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 24, 2025.
This MD&A contains forward-looking statements. See the discussion about these statements under "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" at the beginning of this report.

We are North America's leading provider of the cleanest fuel for the transportation market, based on the number of stations operated and the amount of gasoline gallon equivalents ("GGEs") of renewable natural gas ("RNG") and conventional natural gas sold. We calculate one GGE to equal 125,000 British Thermal Units ("BTUs") and, as such, one million BTUs ("MMBTU") equals eight GGEs. Through our sales of RNG, which is derived from biogenic methane produced by the breakdown of organic waste, we help thousands of vehicles, from airport shuttles to city buses to waste and heavy-duty trucks, reduce their amount of climate-harming greenhouse gases ("GHG") from 60% to over 400% based on determinations by the California Air Resources Board ("CARB"), depending on the source of the RNG, while also reducing criteria pollutants such as Nitrogen Oxides, or NOx. RNG is either delivered as compressed natural gas ("CNG") or liquefied natural gas ("LNG").

As a clean energy solutions provider, we supply RNG (sourced from third party sources and from our anaerobic digester gas ("ADG") RNG joint venture projects with TotalEnergies S.E. and BP Products North America, Inc. ("bp") (see Note 3 to the accompanying consolidated financial statements) and conventional natural gas (sourced from third party suppliers), in the form of CNG and LNG, for medium and heavy-duty vehicles; design and build, as well as operate and maintain ("O&M"), public and private vehicle fueling stations in the United States ("U.S.") and Canada; develop and own dairy ADG RNG production facilities; sell and service compressors and other equipment used in RNG production and at fueling stations; transport and sell RNG and conventional natural gas via "virtual" natural gas pipelines and interconnects; sell U.S. federal, state and local government credits (collectively, "Environmental Credits") we generate by selling RNG as a vehicle fuel, including Renewable Identification Numbers ("RIN Credits" or "RINs") under the federal Renewable Fuel Standard Phase 2 and credits under the California, Oregon, New Mexico and Washington Low Carbon Fuel Standards (collectively, "LCFS Credits"); and obtain federal, state and local tax credits, grants and incentives.

At present, we see the best use of RNG as a replacement for fossil-based fuel in the transportation sector. We believe the most attractive market for RNG is U.S. heavy-duty Class 8 trucking and, based on information from the American Trucking Association and our own internal estimates, we believe there are approximately 4.1 million Class 8 heavy-duty trucks operating in the U.S. that use over 40 billion gallons of fuel per year. As of December 31, 2025, we deliver RNG to the transportation market through over 580 fueling stations we own, operate or supply in 43 states and the District of Columbia in the U.S., including over 200 stations in California. We also own, operate, or supply 27 fueling stations in Canada as of December 31, 2025.

Critically, to generate the Environmental Credits, RNG must be placed in vehicle fuel tanks. We believe our stations and customer relationships allow us to deliver substantially more RNG to vehicle operators than any other participant in the market – we calculate that we have access to more fueling stations and vehicle fleets than all our competitors combined. As of December 31, 2025, we served over 1,200 fleet customers operating over 65,000 vehicles on our fuels.

Over the longer term, we remain committed to RNG, which we believe is a viable, scalable clean fuel solution for medium- and heavy-duty transportation. At the same time, we continue to monitor the development and adoption of alternative use cases and technologies, including hydrogen‑powered and electric vehicles, and we evaluate how our existing assets and capabilities may support these solutions where economically viable. For example, we believe RNG may be used as a feedstock to generate electricity that could support electric vehicle charging and other applications. While RNG remains central to our long‑term strategy, we believe our platform provides flexibility to support a range of lower‑carbon transportation solutions as market conditions, customer preferences, and technology evolve.

We continue to monitor changes in the U.S. Government's trade policy, including the tariffs announced by the U.S. Government in the current year. Trade restrictions and increases in tariffs did not have a significant effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations during the year ended December 31, 2025. The Company does not directly import products from regions subject to significant tariff increases, however we do not know whether, or the extent to which, tariffs may impact our customers, which include fleet owners and operators across all heavy-duty trucking sectors. In addition, tariffs may increase the risk of elevated inflation, which may increase our input costs. The nature of such trade restrictions and tariffs remains unclear. For more information, see "Risk Factors" in Part I, Item 1A of this report.

In recent periods, we have experienced increases in commodity and supply chain costs due to inflationary pressures. The future duration and extent of these pressures and effects are difficult to predict. Although we have partially offset these increased costs through price increases for our products and services, our efforts to manage the current inflationary pressure and to recover inflation-based cost increases from our customers may be hampered by the structure of our contracts as well as the competitive and economic conditions of the markets in which we serve. For more information, see "Risk Factors" in Part I, Item 1A of this report.

As of December 31, 2025, the majority of our debt outstanding represents a long-term loan bearing a fixed rate of interest. Changes in market interest rates do not affect the interest expense incurred from this outstanding long-term debt instrument. However, changes in market interest rates may affect the interest rate and corresponding interest expense on any new issuance of short-term and long-term debt securities. See "Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk" in Item 7A of this report for more information.

paragraphs: Clean Energy Fuels Corp., 一間 Delaware 公司，為美國與加拿大運輸市場提供可再生能源的領導廠商，專注於可再生能源天然氣 ("RNG") 與傳統天然氣的採購與分銷，形式為壓縮天然氣 ("CNG") 與液化天然氣 ("LNG")。RNG 以 CNG 或 LNG 的形式提供，是由非化石燃料來源產生的環境有害廢氣甲烷 ("生物氣") 經過回收與處理後，用以替代化石燃料的運輸燃料，價格可負擔。甲烷是對氣候造成危害的溫室氣體 ("GHG") 中最強大的一種，其對全球變暖的影響約為二氧化碳的 28 倍。我們專注於開發、擁有並營運乳製業 RNG 專案，並向重載與中型商用運輸市場客戶供應 RNG (目前從第三方來源採購)。我們在替代車用燃料產業已有超過 28 年的經驗。我們相信我們處於獨特的優勢，因為環境信用 (如後文所定義) 是由將 RNG 儲存至車輛燃料槽的當事人產生，我們相信我們擁有比任何其他市場參與者更多的儲存設備。
Clean Energy 也將 LNG 與 CNG 的天然氣以批量形式銷售給客戶，包括貨船、太空飛機與大型紙漿廠。

我們相信我們是美國第一家銷售 RNG 作為車用燃料的機構，我們用於此用途的 RNG 銷售量從 2013 年的 13.0 百萬汽油等效加侖 ("GGEs") 增加到 2025 年的 237.4 百萬 GGEs。我們將 1 個 GGE 計算為 125,000 英熱單位 ("BTUs")，因此 1 億英熱單位 ("MMBTU") 等於 8 個 GGEs。我們是北美商用運輸市場提供最清潔燃料的領導廠商，根據我們運營的加氣站數量與服務及銷售的 GGEs 數量，2025 年我們服務與銷售的 RNG (形式為 CNG 與 LNG) 的 GGEs 總計為 468 百萬。由於我們的業務聚焦於 RNG，我們的 RNG 銷售量從 2013 年的車用燃料銷售量的 12% 增加到 2025 年的 88% (排除 O&M (如後文所定義) 服務銷售與非車用銷售的 GGEs)。我們相信在 2025 年，我們提供了加州與美國運輸燃料用 RNG 的 50% 與 32%。

作為一間全面的清潔能源解決方案供應商，我們也在美國與加拿大設計與建造，並運營與維護 ("O&M") 公共與私人車用燃料加氣站；透過 "虛擬" 天然氣管線與連接點運輸與銷售 RNG 與傳統天然氣；銷售我們透過銷售 RNG 作為車用燃料所產生的美國聯邦、州與地方政府信用 ( collectively, "環境信用")，包括根據聯邦可再生能源燃料標準第二階段所產生的可再生能源識別號碼 ("RIN 信用" 或 "RINs")，以及加州、俄勒岡州、新墨西哥州與華盛頓州低碳燃料標準 ( collectively, "LCFS 信用") 下的信用；並取得聯邦、州與地方政府的稅收信用、補助金與激勵措施。我們服務於多種市場的車隊運營者，包括重載貨車、機場、垃圾處理、公共交通、工業與機構能源用戶，以及政府車隊。我們相信這些車隊市場將在可預見的未來繼續為我們的車用燃料提供成長機會。
生物氣是 RNG 的主要來源，是由微生物在無氧環境下分解有機物質時產生。我們的商業規模生物氣來源為厭氧消化氣 ("ADG")，是在密閉罐內分解有機物質如乳製品及其他畜牧廢料所產生，以及垃圾填埋氣 ("LFG")，是由垃圾填埋場中有機廢料分解所產生。

根據 RNG 的潛在成長與正面環境影響，我們的使命是盡可能取得並銷售更多的 RNG 供應。為此，我們認為擁有部分我們需求的 RNG 基設設施是有利的。我們自行進行，也透過與 TotalEnergies S.E. ("TotalEnergies")、BP Products North America ("bp") 與 Maas Energy 的合作夥伴關係進行。此外，我們與知名第三方簽訂長期 RNG 供應買取協議，這些第三方擁有 RNG 生產設施。由於我們的業務將廢甲烷轉化為可再生能源，我們的 RNG 在聯邦與州的計畫下產生環境信用。
根據來源不同，加州空氣資源委員會 ("CARB") 已經判定 RNG 可能具有顯著負的碳強度分數，使我們的客戶能夠實現淨碳負排放的特質。
加州空氣資源委員會 "現行燃料路徑" 2025

目前，我們認為 RNG 最佳的應用為取代化石燃料，主要是柴油，應用在運輸產業。我們認為 RNG 最具吸引力的市場為美國的重型貨車，根據美國卡車協會的資訊與我們內部的估計，我們認為美國約有 4.1 百萬輛重型貨車使用超過 40 十億加侖的燃料。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們透過 582 個我們擁有、營運或供應的加氣站，向運輸市場提供 RNG，這些加氣站位於美國 43 個州與華盛頓特區，包括加利福尼亞州超過 200 個加氣站。我們也擁有、營運或供應 27 個加氣站於加拿大，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。關鍵的是，為了產生環境信用額，RNG 必須被放入車輛的燃料箱中。我們認為我們的加氣站與客戶關係，使我們能銷售比市場上任何其他參與者更多的 RNG 給車輛操作者 – 我們計算我們擁有比所有競爭對手合計更多的加氣站與車輛車隊。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們服務超過 1,200 個車隊客戶，這些客戶擁有超過 65,000 輛車輛使用我們的燃料。我們認為我們是美國唯一一家在加利福尼亞州與全國規模提供 RNG 車輛燃料的公司。
我們的主要產品、服務及其他業務活動如下所述。關於這些活動所產生的收入資訊，請參閱本報告第 7 項 "管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析"。
我們銷售 RNG 與傳統天然氣，以 CNG 與 LNG 的形式作為中型與重型車輛的燃料。

● RNG 會被注入天然氣管線，這讓 RNG 能被運輸至車輛加氣站，於此處可被壓縮並作為 CNG 壓出，也可被運輸至液化設施，於此處被液化並製成 LNG。我們從 DR JV（如後文所定義）取得 RNG，並從 bp 及其他第三方生產者購買 RNG，總計超過 150 個供應來源，通常透過長期 RNG 供應買取協議。為換取 RNG 供應買取協議，我們與供應商協商，以決定雙方各自保留環境信用額價值的百分比。環境信用額的價值基於該信用額被賣給（買取）義務方後的實際價值，或由供應商與我們在協商中同意的價值。我們的供應買取協議為變動性，基於第三方生產者實際生產的 RNG 量，至各個不同最大體積水平。
依協議所規範。2025 年，我們從第三方取得的 RNG 中，40% 為 ADG，60% 為 LFG。
傳統天然氣通常來自當地電力公司或第三方傳統天然氣經銷商。我們透過北美能源標準委員會的基礎合約，以現貨市場或短期期貨指數基礎，或透過買取或支付安排的期貨購買合約購買傳統天然氣，這些合約要求我們購買最低量的傳統天然氣。傳統天然氣以正常購買與正常銷售基礎進行買賣，因為我們購買的傳統天然氣是用來實際交付商品至我們的加氣站，再銷售給客戶。

paragraphs: 下列為管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析（此討論，以及本報告中相同標題之其他定期報告內之討論，均稱為「MD&A」）應與我們經審計之合併財務報表及相關附註說明一併閱讀，且本MD&A內所有對附註之交叉參考均指向該合併財務報表中所識別之附註。本報告之此部分一般討論2025年與2024年項目及2025年與2024年之年對年比較。未包含於本報告中之2023年項目及2024年與2023年之年對年比較，可見於我們2024年12月31日財年年度報告之「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析」，該報告於2025年2月24日提交至SEC。
本MD&A包含前瞻性陳述。請參閱本報告開頭處「對前瞻性陳述之警示」部分之討論。

我們是北美地區在運輸市場提供最乾淨燃料的領導者，根據經營之加油站數量及銷售之可再生能源天然氣（"RNG"）與傳統天然氣之汽油等價量（"GGEs"）計算。我們將1 GGE 定義為125,000 英熱單位（"BTUs"），因此1百萬英熱單位（"MMBTU"）等於8 GGEs。透過我們銷售RNG，此RNG來自有機廢棄物分解產生的生物甲烷，我們協助數千輛車輛，從機場接駁車到市區公車到廢棄與重型貨車，減少其對氣候有害之溫室氣體（"GHG"）排放量，根據加州空氣資源委員會（"CARB"）之判定，減少幅度為60%至超過400%，視RNG來源而定，同時也減少氮氧化物（NOx）等準則污染物。RNG可透過壓縮天然氣（"CNG"）或液化天然氣（"LNG"）方式供應。

作為潔淨能源解決方案供應商，我們提供RNG（來自第三方來源及我們與TotalEnergies S.E.與BP Products North America, Inc.（"bp"）合作之厭氧消化氣（"ADG"）RNG合資計畫）與傳統天然氣（來自第三方供應商），以CNG與LNG形式供應中型與重型車輛；設計與建造，以及營運與維護（"O&M"）美國（"U.S."）與加拿大之公共與私人車輛加氣站；開發與擁有乳業ADG RNG生產設施；銷售與維護用於RNG生產及加氣站之壓縮機及其他設備；透過「虛擬」天然氣管線與連接點運輸與銷售RNG與傳統天然氣；銷售我們因銷售RNG作為車輛燃料而產生之美國聯邦、州與地方政府信用（ collectively, "環境信用"），包括根據聯邦可再生能源燃料標準第二階段之可再生能源識別數（"RIN信用"或"RINs"）及加州、俄勒岡州、新墨西哥州與華盛頓州低碳燃料標準（collectively, "LCFS信用"）之信用；並取得聯邦、州與地方政府稅收信用、補助金與激勵措施。

目前，我們認為RNG最適合用於運輸部門取代化石燃料。我們認為RNG最具吸引力之市場為美國重型貨車，根據美國卡車協會之資訊及我們內部之估計，我們認為美國約有4.1百萬輛重型貨車使用超過40十億加侖之燃料。截至2025年12月31日，我們透過擁有、營運或供應之超過580座加氣站，於美國43個州及華盛頓特區提供RNG至運輸市場，包括加州超過200座加氣站。我們亦於截至2025年12月31日擁有、營運或供應27座加氣站於加拿大。
關鍵在於產生環境信用，RNG必須置入車輛燃料槽中。我們認為我們之加氣站與客戶關係使我們能提供給車輛營運者之RNG遠高於市場其他參與者，我們計算我們擁有之加氣站與車隊數量遠高於所有競爭對手合計。截至2025年12月31日，我們服務超過1,200家車隊客戶，其營運超過65,000輛車輛使用我們之燃料。

長期而言，我們仍致力於RNG，我們認為RNG是中型與重型運輸之可行且可擴展之潔淨燃料解決方案。同時，我們持續監測替代應用案例與技術之發展與採用，包括氫能與電動車，並評估我們現有資產與能力如何在經濟可行之情況下支援這些解決方案。例如，我們認為RNG可作為產生電力之原料，用以支援電動車充電及其他應用。雖然RNG仍是我們長期策略之核心，我們認為我們之平台提供靈活性，以支援各種低碳運輸解決方案，隨著市場條件、客戶偏好與技術之演進。

我們持續監測美國政府貿易政策之變動，包括本年度美國政府所宣佈之關稅。貿易限制與關稅增加對我們之業務、財務狀況與營運結果在2025年12月31日財年期間未產生顯著影響。本公司並未直接進口來自受重大關稅增加影響之地區之產品，然而我們尚不清楚關稅是否會影響我們之客戶，包括各重型貨車運輸部門之車隊所有者與營運者，影響程度亦不確定。此外，關稅可能增加通貨膨脹風險，進而提高我們之投入成本。此類貿易限制與關稅之性質仍不清晰。如需更多資訊，請參閱本報告第一部分，項目1A之「風險因素」。
近來期間，我們因通貨膨脹壓力而經歷了原材料及供應鏈成本的增加。這些壓力與影響的未來持續時間與範圍難以預測。儘管我們已透過產品與服務的價格上漲部分抵銷這些成本增加，但我們努力管理目前的通貨膨脹壓力，並從客戶處回收因通貨膨脹所導致的成本增加，可能受到合約結構以及我們所服務市場的競爭與經濟條件的影響。如需更多資訊，請參閱本報告第一部分第 1A 項「風險因素」。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們大部分未償還的債務代表一項長期貸款，利率為固定利率。市場利率的變動不會影響由此未償還長期債務工具所產生的利息費用。然而，市場利率的變動可能影響任何新發行的短期及長期債務證券的利率及相應的利息費用。如需更多資訊，請參閱本報告第 7A 項「市場風險的量化與質化揭露」。
此績效概覽討論了我們管理層在評估我們財務狀況與營運結果時所關注的事項。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們的成功取決於車隊及其他客戶採用我們車用燃料的意願，這種採用可能不會在預期時間內、預期程度或完全發生。
我們依賴製造商在關鍵客戶及地理市場生產車輛及引擎，而我們對此無控制權。
我們的生物柴油業務可能不會成功。
我們的商業成功取決於我們自身以及第三方供應來源成功開發及運營專案並產生預期數量的生物柴油的能力。
為確保我們開發的新專案產生的生物柴油，我們通常面臨一個長且變動的開發週期，此週期需要大量資源投入，且在我們實現收入前需經過一段長時間的準備期。
畜牧廢棄物及乳製農場專案取決於 LCFS 信用額及 RINs。
我們有虧損的歷史，未來可能產生額外虧損。
任何未來有關氫氣與電動車加氣站的計畫，可能需要大量現金投資與管理資源，且未必符合本公司預期。
RNG、天然氣、原油、柴油、可再生能源柴油及環境信用價格的波動與變動，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
我們面臨來自競爭對手的激烈競爭，許多對手擁有遠較我們為多的資源、客戶基礎與品牌知名度，我們可能無法有效與這些對手競爭。
我們的營運依賴資訊科技，若資訊科技發生重大失敗、不足、中斷或安全問題，可能對本公司業務造成損害。
NG Advantage 可能無法成功。
我們的加氣站建設活動使我們面臨商業與營運風險。
我們與政府機構有重大契約，這些契約面臨獨特的風險。
我們的營運結果有顯著波動，且難以預測。
疫情、疫病或其他傳染性疾病爆發可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司未來的發展將取決於本公司吸引並留住合格的管理、技術及其他人員的能力。
與本公司負債及其他資本資源相關的風險。
本公司可能需要籌措額外資金以繼續支應業務運作，這可能會產生負面影響，且在需要時未必能以可接受的條件或以任何方式取得。
本公司保証準備金可能無法充分覆蓋保証義務，這可能會導致未預期的成本。
與環境健康與安全及政府與環境規範相關的風險
本公司業務受環境、稅務及其他政府規範、計畫與激勵措施影響，這些規範、計畫與激勵措施促進本公司車用燃料的發展，若這些規範、計畫與激勵措施被修改或廢止，可能會對本公司業務產生負面影響。
為受益於環境信用額度，RNG 專案必須進行登記，並接受審計。
paragraphs: 投資本公司涉及高度的損失風險。您應仔細考慮下列所討論的風險因素，以及本報告中包含的所有其他資訊，再做任何有關本公司證券的投資決定。我們認為下列所描述的風險與不確定性是我們面臨最重要的，但還可能有其他風險與不確定性，這些風險與不確定性目前未為我們所知或認為不重要，但後續可能變得重要。這些風險的發生可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果、前景與聲譽造成損害，並可能導致本公司普通股的交易價格下跌。
我們的成功高度依賴於 fleets 以及其他客戶對我們 RNG 與傳統天然氣車用燃料的採用。我們車用燃料的市場在許多領域經歷了緩慢、波動且難以預測的成長。例如，我們車用燃料在重型貨車運輸領域的採用與部署速度比預期來得更慢且範圍更有限。此外，其他重要的 fleet 市場，包括機場、垃圾處理與公共運輸，近年來的成交量與客戶成長較為緩慢，這種情況可能持續。
若我們車用燃料的市場未能以更佳的成長速度或水準發展，或若市場確實發展但我們無法取得市場的重要份額，或市場隨後衰退，將會對我們的業務、前景、財務狀況與營運結果造成損害。

影響我們車用燃料採用的相關因素，許多超出我們的控制範圍，包括但不限於：對使用我們車用燃料的貨車缺乏需求；政府政策、計畫、資金或激勵措施的採用或擴張，或對其他非 RNG 與天然氣車輛或燃料的車輛或燃料的宣傳或流行觀點增加，包括長期支持柴油動力車輛；對柴油、RNG、天然氣或其他車用燃料動力車輛及車隊的排放要求變更；以及對可再生能源柴油、電動與氫動力車輛日益增長的支持；電力公司提供服務的能力限制（例如天然氣電力公司可能無法擴展管線或為新擴張提供服務，電力公司可能缺乏為我們專案提供服務的容量）；對我們車用燃料相對於柴油及其他替代車用燃料的優勢的觀感，包括與供應、成本節省、環境效益與安全等因素相關的考量；原油、柴油、RNG、天然氣及其他車用燃料（如電力、氫氣、可再生能源柴油、生物柴油與乙醇）的供應、需求、使用與價格的增加、減少或波動； fleets 與 fleet 車輛操作者之間的慣性，他們可能無法或不願優先將 fleet 轉換為使用我們車用燃料，而將其置於操作者其他一般業務考量之上，特別是在操作者未因排放規範或其他要求獲得足夠激勵，或缺乏來自客戶、駕駛員或其他利害關係人的轉換需求時；車輛成本、燃油效率、可得性、品質、安全性、便利性（包括燃料與服務）、設計、性能與殘值，以及操作者對這些因素的觀感，通常在我們主要客戶市場中，以及相對於其他燃料動力車輛的考量；適合我們主要客戶市場中使用的車輛（包括重型貨車及其他 fleet）的引擎的開發、生產、成本、可得性、性能、銷售與行銷以及聲譽；車用燃料市場整體的競爭增加，以及此市場中競爭發展的性質與影響，包括其他車用燃料或由這些燃料動力引擎的改進或被認為的優勢；聯邦或州法律、命令或規範對新或額外限制 GHG 排放、"尾氣"排放或內燃機的強制或支持，包括 ACT、2020 年 9 月行政命令、ACF 規範、2025 年 1 月行政命令以及 2025 年 6 月行政命令（如後文所定義）；環境、稅收或其他政府規範的可得性與影響，例如 One Big Beautiful Bill Act（"OBBBA"）、促進我們產品或其他替代品作為車用燃料的計畫或激勵措施，包括我們透過銷售 RNG 作為車用燃料而產生信用額的某些計畫，以及這些信用額的市場價格；以及排放及其他環境規範與壓力，影響我們燃料的生產、運輸與發放。
此外，隨著我們的客戶與合作夥伴因經濟條件（如關稅、政府停擺與市場波動）以及潛在的經濟衰退而反應，他們可能減少支出，並採取額外的預防措施以限制或延後支出，並保存資本與流動性。支出減少、購買決策延遲、缺乏續約、無法吸引新客戶、對業務持續性的不確定性，以及對延長開票條件或價格折扣的壓力，可能會限制我們擴張業務的能力，並對我們的營運結果與財務狀況產生負面影響。

車輛與引擎製造商控制其產品的開發、生產、品質保證、成本與銷售與行銷，這會影響這些產品在市場上的表現、可得性與聲譽。我們依賴這些製造商在目標市場的成功，而我們對他們的活動毫無影響或控制力。僅少數製造商，主要是 Cummins，生產使用我們車用燃料的引擎。製造使用我們燃料的車輛的製造商數量也有限。這些製造商可能決定不擴張或維持，或決定終止或縮減其引擎或車輛產品線，原因可能包括因應美國或對美國的報復性關稅而增加的開發與生產成本，或因應 ACT、2020 年 9 月行政命令、ACF、2025 年 1 月行政命令與 OBBBA 等政府政策或計畫的採用或修改。使用我們燃料的引擎與車輛的有限生產會增加其成本並限制可得性，這會限制大規模採用，並可能降低殘值，這可能會導致操作者對轉換 fleet 為使用我們燃料的車輛產生不願意。此外，一些操作者
